perItemFindings.one_line: `IndepSummandsCLT.prodDesign_clt` is a finite-`FiniteDesign` theorem (`Fintype` coordinate outcomes), so it cannot supply the CLT for records containing schedules drawn from arbitrary continuous law P; `Causalean.Stat.IIDSample.clt_normalizedSum_vec` is the applicable measure-theoretic iid substrate.

perItemFindings.label: prop:raw-pooling-gap

perItemFindings.label: thm:rank-set-coverage-bernoulli

reason: Regression pattern (a) + overarching sufficiency caveat (a stage_1 re-plan is INSUFFICIENT, so rewind to the earliest wrong artifact) — rounds 2 and 3 impose contradictory, unsatisfiable demands on the same node: the F1.5 reviewer requires `lem:weak-compactness-compact-laws` be re-planned as a non-gate reused Mathlib lemma (`MeasureTheory.instCompactSpaceProbabilityMeasure`), while `plan_gate.ts` P9 (tools/src/formalization/plan/plan_gate.ts:391-412) permits only two shapes for a core `status:"cited"` node with `source.carrier=logical-claim`: the deferred `gate:true, gate_class:"cited", lean_kind:"assumption"` form (which then forces the P4 hyp threading the round-2 reviewer rejected as unjustified debt) or a `citation_discharged:true` form that, per the file's own comment at line 385, 'a fresh F1 plan cannot present' (only `bin/gate.ts --discharge` and the substrate-built channel stamp it; `disposition:"reuse"` is additionally excluded at line 399). No legal F1 plan satisfies both checkers, so this is not a mechanical plan bug — the root cause is upstream in discovery/core.json + writeup.tex, where D0 froze a standard textbook fact (Prohorov on a compact metric space, discovery/core.json:2739-2751, writeup.tex:1326-1328, empty `proof_tex`) as a BORROWED citation instead of proving it, even though it is available at the required measure-theoretic abstraction in Mathlib. This overrides the per-boundary heuristic's default of stage_1 for plan_gate violations.
proposed_action: In D0 (incremental repair of the existing conjecture; touch only this node and its provenance): convert core statement `lem:weak-compactness-compact-laws` from `status:"cited"` (empty `proof_tex`, `source.carrier="logical-claim"`, vanDerVaart1998 §2.4) to `status:"proved"` by writing its two-line proof into §7 of writeup.tex at \begin{lemma}[lem:weak-compactness-compact-laws]\label{lem:weak-compactness-compact-laws} (writeup.tex:1326-1328): on a compact metric space every family of Borel probability laws is uniformly tight (the whole space is a compact set of full measure), hence relatively weakly compact by Prohorov, and the set of probability laws is weakly closed; therefore it is weakly compact. Demote vanDerVaart1998 §2.4 from `source` to an ordinary bibliographic reference in the proof text and drop the `source` block from the node so the carrier is no longer `logical-claim`. Change NOTHING else: keep the statement verbatim, keep the node id, and leave `thm:rank-set-coverage-bernoulli`, `thm:rank-set-coverage-cr`, and `thm:uniform-boundary-certificate` (and their `depends_on` lists, writeup.tex:951 and writeup.tex:1039) exactly as they are. After this, F1 may plan the node as an ordinary proved lemma discharged against `MeasureTheory.instCompactSpaceProbabilityMeasure`, P9 no longer applies and the three P4 `logical cited dep must be an explicit hyp` violations vanish without threading the hypothesis.

perItemFindings.label: thm:gaussian-finite-certificate

review.verbatim_critique: Retain `finiteDesignBayesRisk` for the pointwise finite-action posterior minimum, but re-plan the lower-certificate bridge. Define a finite-grid loss whose action type is the subtype of measurable randomized Gaussian selectors, prove locally that its finite-prior Bayes value equals the density-posterior/Tonelli integral, then apply `finiteDesignBayesRisk_le_minimaxValue` once at that selector action type and use the finite-grid-to-full-ball model-class comparison. Do not claim the library theorem can be applied pointwise in the Gaussian observation and integrated. The direct reuse `instCompactSpaceProbabilityMeasure` is a sound clean fit.
